title: Orthogonal basis for a symmetric rational bilinear form
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q$-vector space, meaning that it has a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $B:V\times V\to\mathbf Q$ be linear over $\mathbf Q$ in each variable and symmetric: $B(v,w)=B(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in V$. There exist a nonnegative integer $n$ and a basis $(u_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ of $V$ such that $B(u_i,u_j)=0$ whenever $i\ne j$. The zero-dimensional space and degenerate forms are included.
